capabilities: Render .mw files and mw code blocks as vertical timelines
Edit Markwhen source text and save it in the original format
Filter events by date range and tag
Jump to the first event on or after today
Combine selected .mw files and export a Markdown list (Pro)
disambiguation: Despite the name suggesting a mobile-only tool, the timeline view and source editor are regular Obsidian views that work generally.
extras: Freemium: Combine files, saved filters, and Markdown export require a $5/month or $15 one-time GitHub Sponsors sponsorship; one payment unlocks Pro in all NoteMods plugins. The plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The What's new tab opened after updates suggests other NoteMods plugins and Zovo Chat. The README discloses untested areas (Linux CI, light theme, physical devices, real payments).
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to read a Markwhen plan as a timeline, particularly on phones and tablets, without converting the file to another format.

relations.evidence: The bundled Markwhen parser, version 1.2.0, reads the syntax

summary: Markwhen timeline viewer that renders .mw files and mw code blocks as vertical timelines, with a source editor, date/tag filters, and Pro file combining.
